title: Tidewell Outfitters
headline: A coastal outfitter's site, rebuilt around its field guide
summary: Tidewell's trail and paddling guides drove most of its search traffic, but they lived in a separate blog with no link to the gear. We rebuilt the site around the field guide and connected every guide to the products it mentions.
services: Content strategy and migration, Website design, Raytha development
challenge: Tidewell had two websites: a shop on a hosted ecommerce platform and a field guide on an old blog. The guides brought in most of the organic traffic, but readers had no easy way to find the gear the guides recommended, and the stores' events lived in a spreadsheet.
approach:
We ran a content audit of 420 guides and kept 310. In Raytha, guides, stores, events and gear collections became related content types, so a paddling guide shows the store that runs paddling clinics and the gear list for the trip. The shop stays on its ecommerce platform; the site links into it by product.

The design borrows from nautical charts: a deep teal, a buoy orange and a lot of white space. Every page is server-rendered and weighs under 400 KB before images.
results:
+38%|organic sessions in six months
1.2 s|median page load on 4G
310|guides migrated with redirects
9|stores with their own pages
quote: Our guides finally lead somewhere. Store staff update their own events now, and nobody has to email the web person.

title: Corvane Robotics
headline: Explaining a warehouse robot in under a minute
summary: Corvane's carts were winning pilots, but its website read like a spec sheet. We rebuilt the brand and the site around three plain questions buyers ask first.
services: Brand and identity, Website design, Raytha development
challenge: Operations directors at factories found Corvane through trade shows, then landed on a site full of sensor specifications. Sales spent the first call explaining what the carts actually do.
approach: We interviewed six customers and wrote the site around their questions: what does it move, how does it fit next to people, and how long until it pays for itself. A refreshed identity, a short animated diagram and a resource library with spec sheets for engineers sit on Raytha, with a gated area for partner integrators.
results:
2.4x|demo requests per month
-41%|time to first sales call
12|partner integrators onboarded
AA|WCAG 2.2 conformance
quote: Prospects show up to the first call already knowing what the cart does. That changed our sales cycle.

title: Hollowmere Museum of Craft
headline: Collections online, exhibitions in step
summary: Hollowmere wanted its 6,000-object collection online and its exhibitions, artists and programs connected. We designed a collection browser that curators can maintain themselves.
services: Website design, Raytha development, Content strategy and migration, Accessibility audits
challenge: The museum's collection lived in a database only the registrar could open, and the website was updated by an outside vendor a few times a year.
approach: We modeled objects, makers, materials and exhibitions as related content types and imported the collection with a script that runs again whenever the registrar exports new records. Exhibition pages pull in their objects automatically. The site was tested with screen readers by visitors who are blind or have low vision.
results:
6,100|objects online
48|exhibitions archived
3x|time on collection pages
0|vendor tickets for updates
quote: Curators publish their own exhibitions now. The collection finally feels like ours.
quote_role: Director of collections, Hollowmere Museum of Craft

title: Mosswick Public Library
headline: A library site the whole staff can edit
summary: Six branches, a bookmobile and a seed library, all updated by one person. We gave every branch its own editors and a site that passes an accessibility audit.
services: Content strategy and migration, Website design, Raytha development, Accessibility audits
challenge: Mosswick's website was maintained by one IT generalist. Branch managers emailed changes, events went stale and the site failed a county accessibility review.
approach: We built branches, events, services and staff picks as content types, with user groups so each branch edits only its own pages. The library hosts the site on the county's own servers. Plain language guidelines and a two-hour training got 23 staff editing in the first month.
results:
23|staff editors trained
100%|of templates pass WCAG 2.2 AA
6|branches with their own pages
$0|per-editor license fees
stack: Raytha 2, ASP.NET Core, PostgreSQL, county data center
quote: Every branch updates its own hours and events. The accessibility review came back clean.

title: Kettlerun Coffee Roasters
headline: A wholesale portal for 140 cafés
summary: Kettlerun's wholesale customers called to ask about roast dates and brew guides. We built a members-only area where each café sees its own price list, guides and training videos.
services: Website design, Raytha development, Hosting and care plans
challenge: Café owners needed brew recipes, roast calendars and training material, and Kettlerun's team answered the same questions by phone every week.
approach: The public site tells the roaster's story and sells subscriptions through its existing shop. Behind a sign-in, wholesale customers see roast calendars, brew guides and training videos, with a user group per pricing tier so each café sees the right price list.
results:
140|cafés using the portal
-60%|wholesale support calls
35|brew guides published
1|content model for public and members pages
quote: Our wholesale team used to spend Mondays on the phone. Now cafés just sign in.

title: Sablewood Law
headline: A calm site for a careful firm
summary: Sablewood's clients are families planning for decades. We designed a quiet, readable site with attorney profiles, practice guides and a secure document area for clients.
services: Brand and identity, Website design, Raytha development
challenge: Sablewood had outgrown a template site that looked like every other firm's. Prospective clients wanted to know who they would work with and what the process looks like.
approach: We wrote practice guides in plain language, photographed nothing and illustrated everything, and gave each attorney a profile linked to the guides they wrote. Existing clients sign in to see checklists for their matter type.
results:
+52%|consultation calls
18|plain-language guides
12|attorney profiles
4.8 s to 1.1 s|page load
quote: People tell us the site sounds like we do. That was the whole point.

title: Tallyhook
headline: Docs, changelog and pricing from one content model
summary: Tallyhook's docs, changelog and marketing site were three tools. We moved them into one Raytha site with a shared content model.
services: Content strategy and migration, Raytha development
challenge: Product updates were announced in a changelog tool, explained in a docs tool and sold on a marketing site, and they rarely agreed with each other.
approach: Features, docs articles and changelog entries are now related content types. A feature page lists its docs and the releases that changed it, and the pricing table reads from the same feature list, so it cannot drift.
results:
3 to 1|tools replaced
210|docs articles migrated
-30%|support tickets about how-to
Weekly|changelog, written by product
quote: Product writes the changelog and the docs update with it. No more mismatched screenshots.

title: Wrenfield Family Clinic
headline: Appointments explained, not hidden
summary: Wrenfield's patients wanted to know which location takes walk-ins and which doctors are taking new patients. We put the answers on the home page.
services: Website design, Raytha development, Accessibility audits
challenge: The clinic's old site buried hours, insurance and new-patient status three clicks deep, so the front desk spent hours on the phone.
approach: Locations, providers and services are content types with a new-patient flag that the front desk updates. The home page answers the top five phone questions, and the site links to the clinic's existing patient portal instead of rebuilding it.
results:
-35%|front desk calls
3|locations with live hours
21|provider profiles
AA|WCAG 2.2 conformance
quote: The phones are quieter, and patients arrive at the right location.
